personas.patient: Warm, friendly, low-cognitive load, elderly-friendly, highly accessible. Focuses on clarity and anxiety reduction.
personas.doctor: Clinical, information-dense, analytical. Focuses on efficiency, anomaly detection, and population/patient context switching.

theme_and_context.global_theme: Dual-mode (Patient prefers Light, Doctor prefers Dark/Light dense).

primary.description: Deep Teal. Used for primary actions, prominent text, and trustworthy anchors.

secondary.description: Soft Cyan. Used for active states, subtle highlights, and informational badges.

accent.description: Warm Sand/Terracotta. Used for human warmth in patient UI and 'attention needed' warnings.

patient_recovery_hub.classes: grid grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-12 gap-6 md:gap-8 p-6 md:p-8
patient_recovery_hub.structure: Hero block (NOW) spans 8 cols. Timeline (UPCOMING) spans 4 cols tall. Medicine (NEXT) spans 4 cols.

doctor_command_desk.structure: Sidebar navigation (1 col). Main content (3 cols). Heavy use of border-collapse and 1px borders.

buttons.patient: rounded-full min-h-[48px] px-8 text-lg font-medium shadow-md transition-transform hover:-translate-y-1
buttons.doctor: rounded-md min-h-[36px] px-4 text-sm font-semibold border transition-colors hover:bg-slate-50

cards.patient: rounded-2xl bg-white shadow-lg border border-teal-900/5 p-6
cards.doctor: rounded-lg bg-white border border-slate-200 p-4 shadow-sm

badges.patient: rounded-full px-4 py-1 text-sm font-medium inline-flex items-center gap-2
badges.doctor: rounded px-2 py-0.5 text-xs font-mono border inline-flex items-center gap-1

motion.ai_extraction: Framer Motion scanning line overlay (cyan-500/30 box moving top to bottom infinitely over document) with skeleton text reveals.
motion.staggered_list: Framer Motion variants: initial opacity-0 translate-y-4, animate to opacity-100 translate-y-0, staggerChildren 0.1s.
motion.accessibility: Wrap all motion in 'prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference' media query checks.

accessibility.contrast: Ensure minimum 4.5:1 ratio (APCA preferred). Do NOT use color alone to convey meaning; pair with icons (e.g., triangle for warning).
accessibility.touch_targets: Minimum 48x48 pixels for all interactive elements in Patient UI.
accessibility.testing: All interactive elements MUST have descriptive `data-testid` attributes (e.g., `data-testid="login-submit-btn"`).

images.description: Smiling elderly Indian woman, warm and reassuring

instructions_to_main_agent: Strictly differentiate the visual density between Patient and Doctor views.
Do NOT use HTML native date/select inputs; use Shadcn equivalents configured for large touch targets.
Ensure 'What Changed?' continuity timeline uses clear 'before/after' semantic coloring.
Implement the Accessibility Panel as a floating widget with context API to toggle global CSS classes (e.g., .dyslexia-mode, .high-contrast-mode).
Never use purely transparent overlays over text.
UNIVERSAL_GUIDELINES_FOR_MAIN_AGENT: Do not use generic centered layouts or simplistic gradients.
Create depth through layered design elements with z-index hierarchy.
Do not apply 'transition: all'. Apply specific transitions like 'transition: transform 0.2s ease, opacity 0.2s ease'.
DO NOT center align the app container (.App { text-align: center; }).
Never use AI assistant Emoji characters for icons.
